source.title: Towards Mechanistically Understanding Why Memorized Knowledge Fails to Generalize in Large Language Model Finetuning
source.authors: Lu Dai; Zi-Yang Rao; Yi-Li Wang; Han-Qing Wang; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization during LLM fine-tuning on real-world knowledge-graph tasks, extending grokking-like training dynamics to a different model and data setting.
record.gate_note: The study measures memorization and generalization during fine-tuning, and uses self-patching to test whether relocating representations changes multi-hop accuracy. It does not test small algorithmic datasets, Fourier circuits, initialization scale, weight-norm transitions, critical dataset sizes, or optimizer/numerical artifact explanations. Cited grokking results are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study measures, in realistic LLM fine-tuning on injected knowledge-graph facts, whether multi-hop generalization saturates epochs after memorization (temporal lag, Table 7) or never arrives (multi-fact runs). This bears directly on V4. Its per-epoch self-patching maps also act as a progress measure that partly anticipates generalization (V2). The authors do not frame the result as grokking; they cite grokking only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that fine-tuned LLMs memorize injected facts but often fail to use them in multi-hop reasoning (the Knowing–Using Gap, with an accuracy gap and a temporal lag). They attribute this to knowledge–circuit misalignment: a routing, not capacity, problem. Oracle self-patching recovers much of the lost accuracy, and LRSD improves chaining in all four models tested without hurting memorization. They do not claim the gap is grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Tests real-world knowledge-graph fact injection into fine-tuned LLMs, rather than small algorithmic datasets; uses memorization/generalization accuracy curves and activation self-patching rather than the original grokking setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Task type (chaining versus intersection), fine-tuning scheme (LoRA versus full fine-tuning), and domain/protocol (STaRK-Prime per-fact or multi-fact versus STaRK-MAG multi-fact) change the measured lag and generalization outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Oracle head-entity self-patching at convergence raises chaining accuracy 2.2–6.2× and nearly closes the intersection gap across 6 models and 2 domains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fine-tuned LLMs, failed generalization of injected facts reflects misrouted but present representations that can be recovered by relocating them across layers.

record.problems: The core gap results are reported as averages; Tgen excludes failed cases, and per-fact runs use a limited sample of questions. Self-patching uses an oracle best layer and is described as an upper bound. The gradual dynamics include qualitative figure examples, and the STaRK-MAG non-rise statement is jointly reported for two Qwen models.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted to meet the row cap. LRSD outcomes (Figure 6 and Table 9), its pilot and layer/position controls (Table 10), token-position ablations (Table 3), prompting and irrelevant-patching comparisons (Table 4), and the additional LLaMA irrelevant-patching result (Table 8) are not separately rowed: those induced-method or control results do not directly measure the versions' natural delayed-generalization claims. Figure 7's data-size sweep is not used as evidence for V1 or V5 because it is a knowledge-injection setting and does not test small algorithmic grokking or a critical dataset size.

untested.parts: No small algorithmic datasets and no training-set-size dependence of the delay.
No Fourier or identified generalizing circuit, and no test of later removal of memorizing components. Not tested whether the measure predicts which runs generalize.
No manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm, and no lazy-to-rich transition test. LLM fine-tuning data is assigned to V4.
Weight decay fixed at 0.01; no critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.

missing.what: Plain fine-tuning (λ=0) chaining exact match stays flat at 0.085–0.132 over epochs 30–50 after memorization ≥0.977: no delayed generalization in multi-fact runs.
Multi-fact data-size sweep (Qwen2.5-3B, 10–10,000 facts): memorization 0.98–1.00, chaining 0.08–0.18 whenever ≥100 facts are injected; model-size sweep over LLaMA 1B/3B/8B is similar.
STaRK-MAG intersection accuracy rises together with memorization, ending at 0.93–0.96: no delay.

record.verdict_notes: Tgen is averaged only over runs that reach it, and failed cases are excluded, so the lag figures overstate how often delayed generalization occurs. The delay is epochs-scale and generalization is often never reached: grokking-like only in a weak sense. T01 and T03 identical values match Table 7. Two P-row values were misread (P18, P23). P rows are oracle interventions at convergence and are reassigned to fits_no_version. V3 links removed: the LLM fine-tuning rows fit V4, and no regime switch is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic datasets or training-set-size sweep testing the stated grokking claim.

Tests gradual permeation and whether relocating knowledge representations improves generalization, but not Fourier algorithms or later removal of memorizing components; the progress measure is on injected knowledge in LLMs, not small algorithmic tasks.
Tests delayed generalization on knowledge-graph fine-tuning data, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm or test a lazy-to-rich transition.
Tests fine-tuning only; no LLM pretraining experiment.
Weight decay is fixed in the training protocol; no low-norm mechanism, critical dataset size, or ungrokking test.
Does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax limits as causes of the delay.
